messages:
maria: Quick check — sketching an approach for API keys and project affinity. Do we accept global API keys that map to org-level billing+access, or force project-scoped keys only? Thinking about migration ergonomics and least privilege tradeoffs. :thinking_face:
kevin: FWIW I'd prefer project-scoped by default. Harder to accidentally blast other projects. But we need a smooth migration path for customers with many existing global keys.
oliver: +1 on scoped-by-default. Also want to call out service-to-service workloads — they sometimes need cross-project reads. We should consider an allowlist/intent flag rather than blanket global.
maria: Agree on scoped-by-default. For cross-project reads we could do short-lived exchange tokens via a broker with audited delegation. That keeps long-lived keys scoped.
daniel: How does this interact with RBAC roles? If a key is project-scoped, do we still attach roles to the key principal, or derive allowed routes from the project membership?
kevin: I'd attach roles to the service principal (the key) and make project membership a separate constraint. So effective permission = roles ∩ project-binding. Means you can have the same role in multiple projects but keys are constrained by project binding.
maria: sketch of header/policy example:
```
# example API call
Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_abc123
X-Project: proj-42

# policy (conceptual)
key: sk_live_abc123 -> principal: svc:analytics-processor
principal.roles: [read:datasets, create:jobs]
principal.bound_projects: [proj-42, proj-99]
```
kevin: That model works and keeps checks simple during request time: verify key -> lookup principal -> enforce roles + project membership. Cacheable lookup.
security-bot: Reminder: if you allow a key to list multiple projects, ensure audit logs record which project was requested and which project was allowed. Also rate-limit per-project to avoid noisy neighbor issues. :warning:
maria: Good point — logging per-request, include resolved principal, requested project, decision outcome. We should also emit a metric for cross-project delegation events.
daniel: Migration question: customers today use org-global keys for many things. Proposal: accept global keys but mark them deprecated, add a one-year migrate grace window. During grace, issue advisory logs and an admin console view summarizing where keys are used.
oliver: Make the deprecation visible in token metadata and through the Console UI. Also provide a bulk-scope tool: convert global key -> per-project keys with same roles, and rotate tokens atomically.
maria: Ops concern: if we allow a broker to mint short-lived cross-project tokens, ensure we have quotas and a simple revocation path. Also think about on-prem/private: they may want to keep global keys for operational simplicity. Maybe offer a feature flag for Private deployments.
kevin: Implementation notes:
- storage: principal table keyed by key-id, fields: roles (list), bound_projects (set), org_id, meta tags
- runtime: request verify -> cache principal -> enforce
- migration: background job that scans usages and recommends scoping

maria: Action items:
1) Security to draft audit+revocation requirements (security-bot assigned)
2) Eng to prototype principal table + cache layer (kevin + oliver)
3) Product to draft migration UX for Console (daniel)

maria: Thoughts on timeline? aiming for prototype in 3 sprints, migration tooling following after validation.
kevin: sounds reasonable. :thumbsup:
oliver: I'll start a spike for the broker flow and vault integration.
security-bot: Logged: authn-authz-issue-1777771234 — security will post requirements doc by EOW.
deploy-bot: Reminder: there will be a rolling deploy to staging tomorrow 02:00 UTC that may affect auth-service caches. Please watch the staging dashboard. :rocket:
maria: Nice. If nobody objects I'll open an RFC follow-up with the decisions and attach the sketch above. :eyes:
